title: India’s role in Southeast Asia’s BRICS bet
gist: India's September 2026 BRICS summit in New Delhi showed that Southeast Asian states (Indonesia as member; Malaysia, Thailand, Vietnam as partners) can sit inside BRICS without picking a side, because India's non-anti-Western, G20-affirming 'inclusive multilateralism' balances China and Russia - illustrated by US-ally Philippines attending as ASEAN chair and joining India's CDRI.

insights.claim: Indonesia joined BRICS as a full member and Malaysia, Thailand and Vietnam became partner countries in 2025, meaning four of 11 ASEAN states are now tied to BRICS.
insights.speaker: Yanitha Meena Louis
insights.so_what: BRICS tariff threats from Washington now touch key Southeast Asian export economies.
insights.locator: Southeast Asia’s engagement was another theme

insights.claim: Trump threatened 100% tariffs on BRICS members if they act to undermine the US dollar, raising alarm about Southeast Asian BRICS ties.
insights.speaker: Yanitha Meena Louis
insights.so_what: Tail risk of punitive US tariffs on BRICS-linked ASEAN exporters if de-dollarisation moves advance.
insights.locator: This set off some alarm bells

insights.claim: ASEAN members in BRICS are careful to show they are not taking a side against the West, an approach compatible with India's.
insights.speaker: Yanitha Meena Louis
insights.so_what: Lowers probability ASEAN BRICS members back aggressive de-dollarisation.
insights.locator: But the ASEAN members in BRICS are careful

insights.claim: For Southeast Asia, India's presence in BRICS brings balance, helping shed the perception that the grouping is anti-West or solely China- and Russia-driven.
insights.speaker: Yanitha Meena Louis
insights.so_what: India moderates BRICS' anti-dollar agenda; a key variable for BRICS payment-system ambitions.
insights.quote: India’s presence in BRICS brings balance to the grouping, helping shed the perception that it is “anti-West” or solely China- and Russia-driven.

insights.claim: The BRICS New Delhi Declaration affirmed the G20 as the premier global forum for international economic cooperation, signalling continued relevance of the Global North in Global South mobilisation.
insights.speaker: Yanitha Meena Louis
insights.so_what: BRICS under India is reformist, not a rival to G20/Western institutions.

insights.claim: India maintains functional Western ties via the Quad, the Indian Ocean Rim Association and enhanced EU ties, despite increasingly erratic relations with the United States.
insights.speaker: Yanitha Meena Louis
insights.so_what: India-US friction is a watchpoint; India-EU deepening a counter-trend.
insights.locator: This points to the continued relevance

insights.claim: Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim has stressed India's distinct and influential role within BRICS is particularly important to Malaysia.
insights.speaker: Yanitha Meena Louis
insights.so_what: Malaysia is using India to hedge China within BRICS.

insights.claim: The Philippines, a US treaty ally, attended the New Delhi BRICS summit as ASEAN chair with an understanding this signalled no retreat in its positions toward the US and China; US ambassador Sergio Gor returned to New Delhi to meet President Marcos Jr.
insights.speaker: Yanitha Meena Louis
insights.so_what: Washington tolerates allies' BRICS engagement when routed via India.

insights.claim: The Philippines joined India's Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure as its 71st member on the BRICS summit sidelines, and the CDRI gained BRICS endorsement in the New Delhi Declaration.
insights.speaker: Yanitha Meena Louis
insights.so_what: India's homegrown initiatives are gaining traction as Global South public goods.

insights.claim: India has an Enhanced Comprehensive Strategic Partnership with Vietnam, Comprehensive Strategic Partnerships with Indonesia and Malaysia and a Strategic Partnership with Thailand, with cooperation in semiconductors, defence industry and connectivity.
insights.speaker: Yanitha Meena Louis
insights.so_what: India-ASEAN semiconductor and defence-industry cooperation is a growing investment theme.
insights.locator: India will be a key enabler

insights.claim: India's slow, calculated approach to BRICS will shape how ASEAN as an institution engages with BRICS in the long run.
insights.speaker: Yanitha Meena Louis
insights.so_what: Expect gradual, non-confrontational ASEAN-BRICS engagement rather than bloc alignment.
insights.locator: India’s approach to BRICS has a Southeast Asian flavour
